evidence: At target SHA-256 ba410f6529df2c0ea7e9332a0548c8dd9925ad09cacfae699f5608a39e706276, nn_weight_upload_plan_keeps_model_offsets_and_blob constructs a 512-byte all-zero model.weights value, then checks the resource name, one offset and only upload.bytes.len() == model.weights.len(). NnWeightUploadPlan::from_model currently initializes bytes with Arc::from(model.weights.as_slice()) at current caller SHA-256 05281442479c3328c4de963f45f8f294ec5940b91cfd38187086aeb12520cb2a; this is evidence of the intended copy, not a defect. A same-length wrong payload could pass the current all-zero fixture. The only other NnWeightUploadPlan test use in the repository is gpu/weight_upload/performance_tests.rs at SHA-256 a5845ceb32dfff5a7aa503f267ff568522ec7f880f8b55ac2524c36a1fa32a70, which constructs a zero-filled plan directly and checks Arc::ptr_eq for clones and offset lookups, without invoking from_model or comparing payload contents. The dirty runtime model_asset.rs test SHA-256 54b4fda876f385ed1e6baa5cd4a77710830ff04c0a89d952002423327a6ec6c3 uses an all-zero sample for ZRNN roundtrip equality; the ONNX editor integration test at SHA-256 288ec76413d023fbcaf75bd0cf5efb2e891fb71b83123edeeba1bd874f5fbb1f supplies zero-valued weights and asserts alignment only. CPU interpreter tests contain nonzero numeric weights but verify CPU result vectors, not GPU upload bytes. Repository-wide search for NnWeightUploadPlan, upload.bytes and offset_for_tensor found no other from_model content assertion. This is a coverage TODO only; no production byte corruption is established.
impact_or_question: This test does not establish that from_model preserves a nonzero source payload: same-length replacement or loss of bytes could pass its current all-zero fixture and length assertion.
next_action: Use a distinguishable nonzero weight-byte pattern and assert the upload plan's complete byte payload matches the model blob, while retaining the offset assertions.
